correctness.rationale: The centered unit-edge icosahedron has twelve vertices (0,±1,±φ)/2 and permutations, radius squared (5+√5)/8, and support width w(u)=2h(u). Its twelve vertex-normal spherical pentagons have side inradius sinδ=1/(2R), with sin²δ=(5−√5)/10. Polar integration in five sectors of half-angle α=π/5 has boundary tan θ_b=tanδ/cosψ; integrating cos²θ gives I_C=(5/3)(2α−J), and substitution x=sinψ evaluates J exactly, yielding I_C=π/9+10 sin²δ/(3√3). Multiplying by 12R²/π gives (5+√5)/6+10/(π√3), with 4R² sin²δ=1. Reviewed verify.py: exact Q(√5) coordinates, 30 edges and valency five, plus deterministic numeric quadrature, which is corroborative only. Also checked equivalent term against the complete Platonic table.
